root_cause.text: In `tb_xdomain_copy()`, the `memcpy` length was unconditionally set to `req->response_size` without limiting it to the actual received frame size (`pkg->frame.size`), so a short response causes out-of-bounds read into stale DMA pool data.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `memcpy(req->response, pkg->buffer, req->response_size)` with `size_t len = min_t(size_t, pkg->frame.size, req->response_size); memcpy(req->response, pkg->buffer, len);`, and the commit message explicitly states that "copies req->response_size bytes ... regardless of the actual frame size. When a short response arrives, this reads past the valid frame data ... into stale contents."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a size guard to prevent out-of-bounds read when copying the response payload.
intent_record.what: Replaced direct use of req->response_size in memcpy with a bounded length computed as min(req->response_size, pkg->frame.size) using min_t.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the memcpy now copies at most pkg->frame.size bytes, preventing a read beyond the end of the pkg->buffer if the packet frame is smaller than the expected response size.
